title: Operational Performance Ledger and Deployment-Safe Pinning for Onboarded Models
creator: Aisha Reddy
description: Context: We need an operationalized, auditable ledger for performance artifacts produced during model onboarding that ties a model + version to a signed performance manifest (latency/throughput/cost) and a deployment-safe pin decision. Goal: Make it trivial for runtime, console, and Dedicated teams to discover a model's verified performance signature, its pin-level (e.g., stable/experimental), and the gating criteria used to allow production rollout. This ticket scopes the PM-owned spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and handoffs to engineering/design for UI surface and runtime guards.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical performance manifest schema exists and is stored in the 'performance-ledger' service; manifest includes percentiles (p50/p95), throughput target at X batch sizes, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, and sample input eval snapshot reference.

A deterministic pin decision algorithm is defined and documented (criteria: stability score >= threshold, cost delta <= 15% of anchor model, no regressions on critical evals) with parameterizable thresholds for canary vs stable pins.
The manifest and pin decision are surfaced in Console model pages and available via Redwood API (GET /models/:id/perf-manifest) with versioning metadata and signed attestations.
Runtime can query the ledger and automatically fall back to a compatible variant when a pinned model is unhealthy according to the manifest's SLOs (e.g., sustained p95 > declared p95 for N minutes).
Telemetry: dashboards show number of models with 'stable' pin, recent pin rollbacks, and a sampled cost reconciliation between declared cost and observed cost within a 7-day window.

End-to-end test: onboarding a new model in staging produces a manifest, a pin recommendation, and a deploy can be gated by that recommendation; a canary with shadow traffic shows behavior consistent with declared perf within a 3% margin for p50 and 8% for p95 in 90% of runs.

dependencies: ENG-1842 (runtime fallback hooks and fallback configs)
risks: Incorrect manifest schema could cause runtime mismatches or silent fallbacks; mitigate by schema contract tests and backward compatibility rules.
Overly strict pin thresholds may block healthy models; include staged canary thresholds and manual override path.
Signing/attestation adds operational complexity—requires KMS SLA alignment for Private customers.
Manifest staleness: need refresh hooks and decay/expiration policy to avoid serving based on old performance numbers.

notes: Decisions: use content-addressed storage for manifest payloads and sign the hash to keep manifests small in the ledger.
Fallback policy: runtime will attempt primary pinned model -> variant pool (same family, lower cost) -> fallback to anchor model after N failures.
Consider adding a 'decay window' for manifests (90 days) after which automatic re-verification is required before next rollout.
